thumbnails.concept_ko: 한 줄: 「큰돈이 들어왔는데 동그라미는 전부 가장 싼 칸에 쳐져 있다」. 부천 원미구 중개업소 유리 안쪽에서 본 저층 아파트 단지. verified-data 4절 '중국인이 산 주택의 91%가 6억 이하', '2024년 부천 원미구 817건'이 근거다. 무대가 한국이어야 하므로 유리 경계로 동네를 그대로 담는 현장 장면을 골랐다. 메시지 물리화 채널 = ①형태(빨간 동그라미가 최저가 줄에만 몰림) ④대상 특정("6억") ⑤반응(중개사 표정) ⑥흔적(볼펜으로 그은 동그라미).
thumbnails.prompt_en: COMPOSITION RULE, HIGHEST PRIORITY: the photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with a real scene — never a letterbox band, never an empty panel, never a flat colour block, and never a large expanse of bare empty floor. No face, no hand, no screen and no bright object sits in that bottom three-eighths — every face, hand, sign and key object sits in the upper five-eighths. Counters and table tops run across the MIDDLE of the frame, never near the bottom edge, and anything resting on them sits at mid height. SCALE, EQUALLY IMPORTANT: the Korean estate agent is the largest thing in the picture — his head and shoulders occupy the entire right third of the frame, his face alone spans roughly the top 55 to 60 percent of the frame height, the top of his hair touches the upper edge and is very slightly cropped by it, and his shoulder leaves the frame on the right. Everything outside the window is far smaller, roughly one third of his head height. Photographed from inside a small street-level Korean real-estate agency in Bucheon, camera at standing eye level, looking out through the full-height glass onto a plain 1990s low-rise apartment estate and a row of red-brick multiplex villas under a flat overcast sky. The glass is papered from the inside with dozens of hand-printed listing slips; on the lower rows many of them carry a hand-drawn red ballpoint circle around the price, and every circled slip is one of the cheapest units, one printed clearly with the Korean figure "6억". A worn wooden counter runs across the middle of the frame carrying a cracked red stamp pad, a steel ruler, a chipped stainless cup and a leaning stack of registry photocopies; taped paper notices and a small wall-mounted TV sit behind, wiring tangled along the wall, the floor scuffed. Outside the glass a few passers-by are slightly motion-blurred while the interior stays completely still. On the right a Korean man in his sixties in a grey zip vest with a small agent badge, brow pulled into a deep knot, lips pressed tight, eyes angled down toward the circled slips, one hand flat on the counter. Available daylight from the window mixes with the weak tungsten bulb overhead; a small background shop sign carries Korean lettering as visual texture, small and partly out of focus, exact legibility not required.
